topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing, course overview, and intended learning outcomes for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a multistep disease driven by genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal cellular differentiation, tissue architecture, and growth controls.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumours
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how benign and malignant tumours are differentiated and classified through their tissue invasion, metastatic potential, histological progression, and nomenclature.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the physiological and physical processes by which localized and metastatic tumours cause disease symptoms, organ failure, and death.

topics.label: Tumour incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare patterns of tumour frequency and tissue distribution across human populations and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Cancer screening and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, histological diagnostic criteria, and practical limitations of screening programs for early-stage tumours.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of the learning objectives and reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
